brief: Jensen Huang's personal scandal has reactivated scrutiny of Nvidia's role as the banker of AI: US$42bn in buyouts, US$61bn in equity stakes across 229 startups and 13 public companies, and US$164.5bn in lease guarantees and cloud backstops against US$63.1bn of customer receivables. Interim CEO Colette Kress is seen as more conservative than Huang, which would tighten funding for neoclouds; CoreWeave's stock has corrected 25% and its bonds now yield 15.7% since the story broke. The scandal has also reactivated US national-security hawks, feeding into the Megaspeed GPU-leasing affair and new BIS export-licence rules covering chip transshipment through Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil. With Democrats taking Congress in January, tighter legislation is expected. The bank's base case is that the US has lost the chance to trade chip access for China's rare-earths cooperation, and China is only meeting two-thirds of its Busan pledge. Separately, hyperscaler other income (unrealized AI-stake gains) swung from +US$155bn to -US$9bn quarter on quarter, ex-item net income has been flat for six quarters, the US fiscal deficit keeps widening toward the debt ceiling, and Southeast Asian data-center FDI keeps accelerating, led by Thailand and Malaysia.
